articles.title: ShareChat, Moj partner with Level Infinite to launch - VARIndia.
articles.content: HOME Game ShareChat, Moj partner with Level Infinite to launch India's first-of-its-kind creator-led bespoke gaming micro-drama by VARINDIA 2026-08-19 A first-of-its-kind collaboration bringing together gaming, creator fandom and micro-drama in a single entertainment experience ShareChat and Moj, part of the Mohalla Tech ecosystem have partnered with Level Infinite to launch THE MISFITS, India's first bespoke gaming micro-drama featuring Techno Gamerz, India's most-followed gaming creator with a community of over 50 million subscribers. Level Infinite is Tencent’s global games brand, dedicated to delivering engaging and original gaming experiences to a worldwide audience. Created to mark the launch of Gangstar Mirage City, THE MISFITS is an immersive micro drama blurring the line between gaming, creator fandom and scripted entertainment by placing its story inside the game's universe rather than around it. Set within the world of Gangstar Mirage City, the series moves beyond traditional game marketing by integrating the game's universe into the storyline, offering audiences an immersive entertainment experience led by one of India's most influential gaming creators. The narrative charts the journey of a university freshman who fosters a secret society of outsiders through anonymous digital broadcasts. Scheduled for release on August 20, 2026, the series will stream on ShareChat and Moj, signifying a historic convergence where a global gaming giant, a cultural icon, and India’s burgeoning micro-drama format unite for a single, bespoke entertainment experience. Ahead of the series premiere, pre-registrations for Gangstar Mirage City are officially open on Google Playstore until August 20, 2026, offering fans early access and exclusive in-game rewards. The collaboration also reflects the rapid rise of gaming and micro-drama as two of India's fastest-growing digital entertainment categories. The ShareChat ecosystem reaches over 60 million monthly active users (MAUs) and delivers approximately 900 million daily episode plays, making it one of India's largest destinations for creator-led short-form serialised entertainment. Speaking on the partnership , Neha Markanda, Chief Business Officer, ShareChat and Moj, said, “Micro-dramas are rapidly emerging as one of India's most exciting new entertainment formats, reshaping how audiences discover and engage with episodic storytelling in the vertical format. At ShareChat and Moj, we're excited to be at the forefront of this evolution by creating experiences that bring one of the biggest passions in the country - gaming - alongside creators, brands and storytelling in an innovative way under one roof. THE MISFITS is a strong example of this vision, combining the scale of Techno Gamerz, the immersive world of Gangstar Mirage City, and the power of the ShareChat ecosystem to create a first-of-its-kind gaming micro-drama. As brands look for more authentic and engaging ways to connect with their digital-first audiences, we believe collaborative micro-dramas will play an increasingly important role in the future of entertainment and brand storytelling.” Sidharth Arora, IN Country Manager of Level Infinite added, "Gangstar Mirage City has been built around immersive storytelling, so we wanted its launch to reflect that same philosophy. Partnering with ShareChat, Moj and Techno Gamerz enabled us to introduce the game through an original narrative that...

articles.title: iQOO Announces ₹40 Lakh Hackathon for AI and Mobile Innovators - digital terminal
articles.content: iQOO has announced the launch of iQOO Hackathon 2026, India’s first hybrid mobile hackathon, inviting engineers, young developers, AI enthusiasts and early IT professionals across India to build technology solutions for real-world challenges. With registrations now open, the hackathon will travel across Bengaluru, Pune, Chennai, Hyderabad. The four-city City Battles will follow a 30-hour format, challenging participants to rethink conventional development workflows by combining smartphones with traditional development environments. The initiative will culminate in a Grand Finale in Bengaluru, where the winning teams from the city battles and shortlists from the online registrations will compete for the coveted title of iQOO Hackathon 2026 Champion. Going beyond a conventional hackathon, iQOO Hackathon 2026 introduces a phone-first, hybrid development model. Putting the performance capabilities of the iQOO 15 to the test, challenging participants to code, build and solve complex problems using their phone as part of their development workflow. The experience is enabled by the combination of a powerful Snapdragon processor and OriginOS optimisation, supporting faster coding, seamless multitasking and demanding workloads. The device’s vapour cooling system helps manage heat during prolonged, intensive usage, while its large-capacity battery supports long hours of development without frequent charging; bringing together the performance, endurance and efficiency required by IT professionals, coders and engineering students. The Red Light, Green Light format challenges participants to build primarily on the iQOO smartphone during the Red Light phase, while the Green Light phase allows them to combine smartphone and laptop workflows. Participants will also receive AI credits, with projects judged on phone-first execution, AI integration, Office Kit usage, real-world relevance and final pitch quality Selected participants will have access to 12+ industry mentors throughout the hackathon. Their projects will be evaluated by a panel comprising technology leaders and AI experts with participants assessed on the quality and relevance of their solutions, technical execution, creativity and ability to address real-world challenges. The City Battles will kick off in Bengaluru on August 29-30 , followed by Pune on 5-6 September, Chennai on 12-13th September and Hyderabad on 26-27 September . Winners from each city will progress to the Grand Finale, scheduled to take place in Bengaluru on 9-11th October. The competition will offer a ₹6 lakh prize pool at each City Battle, with awards for the Winner, First Runner-up, Second Runner-up and Special Honour, alongside additional recognition for standout projects. The Grand Finale will feature a ₹25 lakh prize pool, giving participants an opportunity to compete at the national level and earn the title of iQOO Hackathon 2026 Champion. With iQOO Hackathon 2026, the brand aims to demonstrate how iQOO makes high performance smartphones that extend beyond everyday use to support demanding professional workflows. By putting coders and developers through intensive, real-world challenges, the hackathon showcases how performance, software optimisation, cooling and battery endurance can come together to support long-duration, complex tasks. articles.title: Indian MSMEs Need an AI Rework Budget Before Automation Scales - SMEStreet
articles.content: IoT & AI Technology For SMEs Indian MSMEs Need an AI Rework Budget Before Automation Scales Small firms face tight budgets, limited specialist talent and intense pressure to show a return quickly. Those realities make hidden rework more dangerous, not less. A large company may absorb a week of cleanup across several departments. SMEStreet Edit Desk 19 Aug 2026 16:33 IST Follow Us New Update Listen to this article 0.75x 1x 1.5x 00:00 / 00:00 Article by Gleb Tsipursky For an Indian micro, small or medium enterprise, the business case for artificial intelligence is easy to understand. A small team can answer customer questions, prepare quotations, reconcile invoices, screen job applications and produce marketing material faster than before. The harder question is whether the apparent savings survive the correction work that follows. That hidden labor deserves its own line in the budget. Before an MSME scales an automated workflow, it should set an AI rework budget: a defined allowance for checking outputs, correcting records, reversing actions, handling exceptions and repairing customer trust when the system gets something wrong. SMEStreet's coverage of AI, skills and digital adoption in Indian SMEs has highlighted both the opportunity and the constraints. Small firms face tight budgets, limited specialist talent and intense pressure to show a return quickly. Those realities make hidden rework more dangerous, not less. A large company may absorb a week of cleanup across several departments. In a ten-person enterprise, the same mistake can consume the founder's attention, delay collections and disrupt customer service at once. Consider an AI assistant that prepares sales quotations. The first dashboard may show that preparation time fell from 30 minutes to five. Yet the real cost may include a manager checking unusual terms, an employee fixing product codes, a finance worker correcting tax treatment and a salesperson explaining an error to the customer. If those minutes are not counted, the firm may scale a workflow that looks productive while quietly moving labor into less visible places. AI as Priority in India The Government of India is promoting AI and digital adoption among MSMEs through the IndiaAI Mission and related initiatives. That support can expand access to tools, compute, skills and financing. But adoption metrics should be paired with evidence about dependable use. A business becomes more capable not when it activates more software, but when it can use the software without creating uncontrolled correction work. A rework budget can be simple. For each automated workflow, the owner should track six categories for 30 days. First, verification time: how long employees spend checking outputs before use. Second, correction time: how long they spend fixing wrong or incomplete results. Third, reversal time: the effort required to restore the prior state after an automated action. Fourth, exception time: work created by cases the system cannot handle. Fifth, coordination time: messages, meetings and handoffs needed to resolve the problem. Sixth, trust repair: refunds, follow-up calls, rewritten communications or other work needed after a customer or employee is affected. Efficient Optimisation...

articles.title: Exicom's EV Charger Breakthrough: India's First Liquid-Cooled Power Modules Hit Production
articles.content: home News Exicoms ev charger breakthrough indias first liquid cooled power modules hit production Exicom’s EV Charger Breakthrough: India’s First Liquid-Cooled Power Modules Hit Production Exicom Tele-Systems has begun manufacturing liquid-cooled AC and DC power modules in Hyderabad, becoming the first Indian company to produce the technology for international EV charging markets Outlook Business Desk Curated by: Gowri Lakshmi Published At: 19 August 2026 4:03 pm Published At: 19 August 2026 4:03 pm SUBSCRIBE Photo: AI generated Summary of this article Exicom has started producing liquid-cooled power modules for AC and DC EV chargers at its Hyderabad facility, initially for Tritium’s charging systems. Liquid cooling keeps components around 10°C cooler than conventional air-cooled systems and offers greater protection against moisture, dust and salt air. Initial production will serve North American and European markets, before the technology is incorporated into Exicom’s domestic charging solutions. Exicom Tele-Systems announced Wednesday the start of manufacturing liquid-cooled AC and DC power modules at its Hyderabad plant, as reported by Economic Times. This makes the firm the first in India to build such power electronics for international markets. The initial batch of these modules will power Tritium's DC-FLEX charging systems and TRI-FLEX ultra-fast DC chargers. Addressing Thermal Challenges High temperatures remain a primary hurdle for high-power electric vehicle infrastructure. Thermal stress triggers almost 60% of power electronics failures. A temperature spike of 10°C to 15°C can double component failure rates, the company stated. 1 August 2026 Get the latest issue of Outlook Business Liquid-cooled configurations maintain internal temperatures about 10°C lower than traditional air-cooled setups. They utilise a sealed architecture, shielding critical components from salt air, moisture and dust. articles.title: Inflexor Ventures leads Rs 65 Cr investment in Butterfly Learnings to transform paediatric ...
articles.content: August 19, 2026 | Wednesday | News Butterfly Learnings (Bombay Autism Services), India's first full-stack paediatric behavioural health platform for neurodivergent children, has raised Rs 65 crore in its Pre-Series B funding round, led by Inflexor Ventures, with continued participation from existing investors Insitor Partners and Enzia Ventures, reaffirming their conviction in the company's long-term growth. The fresh capital will be used to expand Butterfly's centre network across India, strengthen its technology platform, and commercialise its breakthrough early autism screening solution. Nearly 45 million children across the country are estimated to live with conditions such as Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), ADHD and learning disabilities, yet only a small percentage receive timely intervention. Delayed diagnosis, fragmented care pathways and a shortage of trained specialists continue to prevent children from receiving support during the most critical years of brain development. Mumbai-based startup Butterfly Learnings is the only BHCOE (Behavioural Health Center of Excellence) a ccredited therapist training institute in Asia, reflecting its commitment to globally recognised standards of behavioural healthcare delivery. A key differentiator for Butterfly Learnings is Get SET Early, a patented eye- tracking autism screening technology for which the company holds an exclusive global licence. Following CDSCO approval, the solution enables autism screening in children as young as one year old, helping reduce diagnostic delays and enabling earlier intervention. The newly raised capital will support Butterfly Learnings' expansion from being predominantly focused on Maharashtra to other geographies in India, strengthen its digital and AI capabilities, scale the deployment of Get SET Early through hospitals and pediatricians, and expand its in-house therapist training programme. Looking ahead, Butterfly Learnings plans to deepen its presence across India, strengthen partnerships with hospitals and paediatricians, expand access to inclusive education, advance AI-enabled precision care, reinforcing its mission of making high- quality neurodevelopmental care accessible to families across India.

articles.title: Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train: India's First High-Speed Rail Corridor Advances With 359 ...
articles.content: Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project is progressing steadily with significant gains recorded across viaducts, track infrastructure, electrification, bridges and tunnels, according to the latest progress update released by National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL). The NHSRCL is the implementing agency for the 508-km Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor, which is the first bullet train project in India. According to the agency's July progress update, pier work has been completed over 453 km and viaduct construction has been undertaken over 359 km. Meanwhile, Reinforced concrete (RC) track bed construction has been completed over 215 km, while 91 km track slabs have been laid with Cement Asphalt Mortar (CAM) injection completed. The electrification infrastructure has also expanded with over 9,000 Overhead Equipment (OHE) masts installed across 200 km of the bullet train corridor, according to the update. These masts will form part of the overhead traction system required to supply power to high-speed trains. Noise barriers have been installed along 297 km of the alignment to reduce the transmission of noise generated during high-speed train operations. A total of 17 river bridges and 15 steel bridges have been completed for the project. Tunnel construction in Maharashtra has also moved ahead. According to the NSHRCL update, four mountain tunnels have been excavated, while 5 km of tunnel constructed using the NATM method has also been completed. The corridor, which is India's first bullet train project, will connect Mumbai and Ahmedabad through 12 stations across Maharashtra, Gujarat and Dadra and Nagar Haveli. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw had earlier announced that India’s first bullet train will begin its inaugural 100-km run between Surat and Vapi in August 2027, The New Indian Express reported . The section is part of the larger 508-km Mumbai–Ahmedabad high-speed corridor, also known as Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project, which is expected to be fully operational by 2029. Vaishnaw said the Mumbai–Ahmedabad travel time would drop to 1 hour 58 minutes once the corridor is ready. He added that the first operational run in August 2027 would be limited to the 100-km Surat–Vapi stretch. "A significant milestone is that the bullet train will cover the distance between Ahmedabad and Mumbai in just 1 hour 58 minutes upon the completion of the high-speed rail corridor. The inaugural run in August 2027 will cover 100 km between Surat and Vapi," Vaishaw said. The minister said trains on the 508-km corridor will operate at speeds of up to 320 kmph. With four stops, the Mumbai–Ahmedabad trip will take 1 hour 58 minutes, while halting at all 12 stations will extend the journey to 2 hours 17 minutes. "The bullet train will cover the distance between Mumbai and Ahmedabad in 1 hour 58 minutes with four stops. However, if it halts at all 12 stations, the total journey time will be 2 hours 17 minutes,” Vaishnaw said. The corridor will be opened in phases, covering the Vapi-Surat, Vapi-Ahmedabad, and Thane-Ahmedabad stretc h es before the Mumbai-Ahmedabad section becomes operational in the final stage. articles.title: India's FIRST 14-metre acoustic-transparent 4K LED cinema screen opens in Kochi
articles.content: India’s FIRST 14-metre acoustic-transparent 4K LED cinema screen opens in Kochi Edited By: Riya Ashok Madayi India's first 14-metre acoustic-transparent Direct View 4K HDR LED cinema screen was unveiled at Magic Frames in Kakkanad, Kochi. Photo | Special Arrangement A new cinema screen in Kochi is bringing a technology not previously installed at this scale in India. Magic Frames in Kakkanad has unveiled a 14-metre acoustic-transparent Direct View 4K HDR LED cinema screen, making it the first installation of its kind in the country. The screen is part of MAGNOVA, a premium large-format cinema offering from UFO Cinema Solutions, powered by HEYLED technology. The installation measures 14 metres by 6 metres and uses a DCI-compliant Direct View LED display with 4K HDR capability and a 3.91 mm pixel pitch. Unlike a conventional projection setup, where an image is projected onto a screen, a Direct View LED system produces the image directly through the display itself. What makes the screen different? The key technology behind the Kochi installation is its acoustic-transparent architecture. ALSO READ: Nivin Pauly's 'Bethlehem Kudumba Unit': Malayalam cinema's ultimate onam package? In a conventional LED cinema screen, placing speakers directly behind the display can be a challenge because the screen itself can obstruct the path of sound. The MAGNOVA installation has been designed to allow cinema speakers to be positioned behind the 14-metre-wide LED display. This means the audio can originate from behind the image, aligning the source of the sound with what appears on screen. The setup is paired with Dolby Atmos immersive audio and Pulz Cinema Speakers. The acoustic-transparent architecture allows cinema speakers to be positioned behind the LED display. Photo | Special Arrangement The display also offers 4K HDR presentation, along with the characteristics associated with Direct View LED technology, including high brightness, contrast and the absence of projector-based light spill. The technical specifications at a glance- The MAGNOVA screen installed in Kochi features: Screen size: 14 metres x 6 metres Display technology: Direct View LED Resolution: 4K HDR: Yes Compliance: DCI-compliant Pixel pitch: 3.91 mm Technology: Powered by HEYLED Audio setup: Dolby Atmos Speakers: Pulz Cinema Speakers Key feature: Acoustic-transparent LED architecture allowing speakers to be placed behind the screen The installation represents a different approach to theatrical presentation, combining a large-format LED display with an audio configuration designed around speaker placement behind the image. From projection to Direct View LED Cinema technology has moved through several display formats, from film projection to digital projection, while Direct View LED has emerged as another option for theatrical exhibition. The 14m x 6m MAGNOVA display uses Direct View 4K HDR LED technology with a 3.91mm pixel pitch. Photo | Special Arrangement With a Direct View LED system, the display itself produces the image instead of relying on a projector and reflected light. The Kochi installation combines this display technology with an acoustic-transparent design, addressing the placement of speakers behind a large LED cinema screen. articles.title: Bengaluru To Host India's First Happiness Summit - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Cities Bangalore Bengaluru To Host India’s First Happiness Summit Bangalore Urban news Bengaluru To Host India’s First Happiness Summit By UrbanPost August 19, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bengaluru To Host India’s First Happiness Summit Bengaluru is set to host India’s first World Happiness Summit, bringing policymakers, researchers, business leaders and wellbeing practitioners together to examine how quality of life can become a more measurable part of development. The event is expected to place issues such as mental wellbeing, social connection and inclusive growth alongside conventional indicators of economic progress. The summit comes as Indian cities face a growing gap between economic expansion and everyday liveability. Bengaluru remains one of the country’s strongest technology and employment centres, but rapid growth has also intensified pressure on housing, transport, public spaces and basic urban services. These factors directly shape how residents experience the city. The concept of urban wellbeing extends beyond individual happiness. Access to safe streets, affordable housing, reliable public transport, clean air, green spaces and essential services can influence physical and emotional quality of life. For a rapidly expanding city, these factors are closely linked to whether economic growth remains inclusive. Bengaluru provides a particularly relevant setting for that discussion. Its large technology workforce and expanding business districts have generated employment and investment, while long commuting times, traffic congestion and rising living costs have become persistent concerns for many residents. A city can therefore perform strongly in economic indicators while producing uneven experiences of urban life. Urban planners increasingly use broader measures of liveability when assessing development. Public spaces, walkability, access to nature and social infrastructure can affect how residents interact with their neighbourhoods. These considerations are also relevant to climate resilience, as trees, shaded streets and well-designed public areas can reduce heat exposure while improving everyday comfort. The summit’s value will ultimately depend on whether discussions translate into measurable approaches that cities can use. Wellbeing indicators could potentially complement conventional measures such as investment, employment and infrastructure delivery, giving policymakers a clearer picture of whether growth is improving everyday life. There is also an economic case for this approach. Cities that provide healthier and more accessible environments can improve workforce productivity, attract talent and strengthen social cohesion. Businesses increasingly consider quality of life when employees choose where to live and work, making urban wellbeing part of the wider competitiveness equation. For Bengaluru, the event offers an opportunity to connect its economic ambitions with the lived experience of residents. The challenge will be moving the conversation beyond the language of happiness and towards practical improvements in housing, mobility, public spaces, environmental quality and access to services. If those links are made effectively, the summit could contribute to a broader understanding of urban success—one in which a city’s progress is judged not only by its economic output, but also by how safely, affordably and comfortably people can live within it.
